correctness.rationale: The edge gradient space is exactly the subspace where all terminal-path edge sums agree. Orthogonal least squares adjusts every edge in a path by the same amount; minimization of the common sum gives the displayed projection entries. Their signs are fixed and summing rowwise absolute values gives the exact induced endpoint norm. If the distinguished path has length t and k other paths totaling M edges, Cauchy–Schwarz gives reciprocal-length sum at least k²/M, yielding row sum at most 3 + (1/2)sqrt(N/s). One s-edge path and floor(sqrt((N-s)/s)) balanced long paths have reciprocal sum tending to 1/s and give the matching leading term 1/(2sqrt(s)). A standalone exact-rational implementation independently inverts reduced incidence Gram matrices and checks 21,580 representative equalities; it does not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The maximum transfer-current ℓ1 column/row length is a natural worst-edge sensitivity measure, governing congestion for electrical oblivious routing. The result supplies an exact rational value for every parallel-path network, and the sharp structural threshold 1/(2sqrt(s)) for every fixed minimum edge subdivision s. Distinguishing the shortcut case s=1 from s≥2 in entire infinite families requires both the all-profile projection calculation and a matching extremal inequality; it is not the previously known balanced shortcut lower example or a routine relabeling.
